newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers see moderate growth ahead - D&B.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers see moderate growth ahead - D&B.

text.p: U.S. manufacturers expect their sector to expand at a significantly slower pace in the next three months ahead, according to The Dun & Bradstreet Corp's survey of 1,000 manufacturing executives.
The respondents also reported slower growth in production and new orders during the past three months, the survey said.

Dun & Bradstreet said its industrial sentiment index dropped nine points to 18, driven by declines in almost every key measure of industrial optimism. The index registered 27 in April, 26 in March and 18 in May 1996.
The D&B manufacturing production index dove to 41 in May versus 59 in both April and March and 38 a year ago.
The new orders index fell 20 points to 40 in May, against 60 in April, 59 in March and 39 in May 1996.

Despite the steep decline in business optimism, the manufacturing sector is still performing well ahead of last year, and expectations are on par with last May's projections, said D&B chief economist Joseph Duncan.
Nevertheless, Duncan said that manufacturers reported that their sector is ready to "slow to more sustainable levels" after a full quarter of rapid expansion.

"Manufacturing executives say they are taking early steps to bring down inventories and scale back production levels, and that they will be less aggressive about hiring new employees than previously expected," Duncan said.
However, almost half of the survey respondents said they expect new orders to increase in August, he said.
